dossier.headline: The RBI raised the repo rate to 5.50%, its first hike since February 2023
dossier.summary: The MPC met 5–7 October with most economists expecting 25 basis points, and the market trimmed risk in the half hour before the decision. The RBI delivered a unanimous 25 bp hike to 5.50% and moved its stance to 'calibrated tightening', the first increase since February 2023, while lifting its FY27 inflation forecast to 5.2%. Governor Sanjay Malhotra signalled the next move would be a hike or a pause. It has not appeared since 7 October.
why_it_matters: The policy rate sets the cost of money for the rate-sensitive sectors the notes track.
A raised inflation forecast shapes expectations for the following meetings.
The stance change marks a turn after a long easing and hold period.
